messages:
maria: quick check — we're sampling user prompts for evaluation. are we allowed to keep raw prompt text for 90 days for model tuning?
kevin: tagging @diane @sam :eyes: my gut: we should avoid storing raw prompts with potential PII long-term. what's the current default retention?
diane: prod default is 7 days for raw prompt samples. anything beyond that needs a data-privacy approval and a documented justification. short answer: no 90d without approval.
sam: legal note: if prompts can include PII or PHI, we need either explicit consent or to store only non-identifying artifacts (embeddings, lengths, hashed tokens with a salt). Also make sure Authorization headers are never logged.
maria: ok — for the immediate PR i'm planning a feature-flagged toggle so SRE/dev can flip sampling off. example config i was thinking to add:
```
prompt_sample:
  enabled: true
  mode: "raw" # raw | hashed | metrics_only
  retention_days: 7
  sample_rate: 0.01
  obfuscate_headers: ["authorization", "cookie"]
```
kevin: SGTM. recommend default `mode: "metrics_only"` for hosted, and `hashed` for dedicated after opt-in. for `hashed` we need server-side salt (env var) and a scrubber for emails/phones before hashing.
diane: i'll drop the common scrub regexes in a gist — basic rules: remove emails, phone numbers, SSNs, and short ids before hashing. also add a test that verifies `obfuscate_headers` covers Authorization and Cookie.
sam: also add a policy line: any retention >30d requires a dataprivacy ticket + legal signoff. saves us from last-minute audits.
maria: thanks. i'll create the PR and set feature flag off by default. tagging @kevin for review when ready.
kevin: cool. for the PR add a small e2e that ensures prompt text is blanked when `mode: metrics_only`. quick snippet for obfuscation logic if helpful:
```
function scrubAndHash(prompt, salt) {
  const scrubbed = prompt.replace(/\b[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.-]+\b/g, "<EMAIL>")
                         .replace(/\b\d{3}[-.]?\d{2}[-.]?\d{4}\b/g, "<SSN>");
  return hash(scrubbed + salt);
}
```
maria: perfect. i'll include that and add tests. one more Q: are we allowed to store small raw samples for internal debugging if access is limited to a small team?
diane: only if access is role-restricted and logged, and you still need dataprivacy approval for retention >7 days. short-lived debug dumps (<24h) are usually ok if ephemeral and rotated.
redwood-bot: data-privacy-policy v2 accepted by legal on 2025-02-10 — see https://redwood/docs/data-privacy for details :lock:
maria: got it, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
